subject: [NimbleHealth] SDK request-id mismatch causing telemetry split
messages:
From: Jamie Lin <jamie@nimblehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC - inconsistent request ids in SDK (NimbleHealth)

Hi Marissa / team,

We started a short POC with the SDK yesterday and are seeing request IDs that differ between the edge client traces and the tokens reported in Redwood's telemetry. The mismatch is causing our downstream billing/usage dashboards to show split sessions, which makes it impossible for our ops team to reconcile usage for our trial customers.

Attached is a compressed trace excerpt (nimble-poc-trace-20270814.log.gz) and the SDK config we're using (nimble-sdk-config.json). The pattern: same client call produces two different request-id values on subsequent retries (we're using the default retry=2).

Can your eng team help triage urgency? We have an internal demo next Tuesday and would prefer a short-term mitigation if a full fix needs more time.

Thanks,
Jamie Lin
Product Ops, NimbleHealth

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: POC - inconsistent request ids in SDK (NimbleHealth)

Marissa / team — initial triage notes below. I've attached the minimal repro we used to replicate with our local agent.

Observed behavior:
- With client retry enabled (retry=2) we see the SDK generate a new request-id header for each retry attempt (header: x-rw-request-id). The runtime uses the first-seen request-id as the canonical key for token attribution. When a retry arrives with a different ID, the runtime attributes tokens to the later ID and the telemetry shows split sessions.
- The SDK has a race in the retry path where a fresh UUID is generated per attempt rather than preserved from the original call context. The race only reproduces under short TCP hiccups we simulated.

Root cause: SDK-side regeneration on retry. Not a kernel/runtime corruption.

Immediate plan (48–72h):
1) SDK shim: add a short patch to preserve request-id across retry attempts. This is a small change in the client request builder and passes unit tests. Can produce a patch release (v1.3.2) within 24–48 hrs.
2) Canary: we can cut a canary build and route 5% of NimbleHealth traffic to it; runtime changes not required. Jonas, can you set up a canary route and monitor request-id stability?
3) Docs: quick note for Sales/CS about the mitigation and the recommended temporary config (set retry=0 if customers want an immediate stopgap).

Impact/Risk: low for the SDK change. Rolling back is just a client-side version bump.

I'll work overnight and push a draft PR.

-Karthik
Lead Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
